name: Definite
long_description:
Definite connects operational data with finance so businesses that make, move, build or operate things can see what each production run, load and job actually cost.

These businesses already record a lot: production runs, shipments, job sites, equipment hours, work orders. Finance records the same business in a different shape. Operating systems track activity by site, line, or day. The ledger tracks it by entity, account, and month. Both sets of records exist, but the link between an operating decision and its financial effect usually lives in spreadsheets and in a few people's heads.

So questions that should be routine take days. What happens to cash if one plant adds a shift? How does a change in throughput or staffing flow into the forecast? Which operating changes actually moved the numbers last quarter?

Definite connects to existing operational and financial systems read-only. Models propose how operational records map to financial ones and explain what they find. Deterministic rules perform the calculations and checks, so results trace back to the source records they came from. 

Definite started in a plant office an hour from campus, watching a controller rebuild the same spreadsheet she rebuilds every month to tie her production system to her ledger. The three of us met at the University of Waterloo and had each spent our careers on a version of that join. Gurshabd built wallet policy and approval controls at BitGo, where proving customer assets matched the ledger was still done by hand. Farhan built recommendation systems for Instagram Reels at Meta, joining billions of raw events to the numbers the business reported. Mazin built trading systems at Optiver, then agents for financial analysts at Boosted.ai, where analysts would not act on a number they could not trace. In finance that work is at least funded. In companies that make and move things, nobody had built it at all.
one_liner: Connect operational data with finance to see what drives the numbers.

name: SPITA Labs
long_description: Robots and servers need more power and data every year, and both still get it through tangles of cables and custom PCBs. A typical robot is a pile of boards wired together by hand, and every design change means waiting on a new board. SPITA is building networking for power. SPARC is a backplane with plug-in cards: drop in a chip or module, and software sets whether each pin carries power or data. Nothing needs rewiring or a new PCB. Once the design works, we export the schematic for production. We're starting with robotics teams, who can test new designs without spinning a board. Next is the server rack, where the same approach replaces today's cable-heavy backplanes.
one_liner: Networking for power and data in robots and servers

name: Luminary
long_description:
Luminary is an AI CEO that leads human and agent teams on company-wide missions. We're building the complete infrastructure for a fully AI-native company, starting with a world model of how your business works and building up to an AI CEO that can lead it.

Today's AI tools are good at automating the work they're handed, but they still wait to be told what to do next. So even with the abundance of AI agents, companies are still bottlenecked by leadership and vision. Someone has to decide what's worth building, rally the right people behind it, and bring it to market.

Luminary takes on that job. Instead of asking it to build a feature, you hand it part of your business to grow. It then proactively discovers opportunities, plans high-impact missions, and leads your people and its own agent swarms to accomplish them. 

Some examples of audacious missions it can execute:

- Launch a product: It spots customers building the same workaround, makes the business case, directs coding agents to build it, and rolls it out.
- Enter a new market: It finds an unexpected group of buyers, reworks positioning and pricing around them, and wins the first accounts.
- Rescue a stalled deal: It notices an enterprise deal losing momentum, designs a new strategy with your sales team, and gets it signed.

Under the hood, Luminary builds a living world model and follows a leadership constitution that shapes every call. Proprietary evals check every deliverable, and a recursive self-improvement loop turns each mission into institutional wisdom.
one_liner: AI CEO that leads human & agent teams on company-wide missions

name: Vibe Robotics
long_description:
Vibe Robotics builds robots for the work nobody should have to repeat.

We’re starting in hotels. Every day, housekeeping teams move linens between floors, restock carts, and fold stacks of laundry before the next guests arrive. It’s physical work that has to get done every shift.

Our first robot, Vibe 01, folds a hand towel fully autonomously in 23.8 seconds. It learned from just a few hundred human demonstrations. We’re piloting Vibe 01 at a Hilton property and working with hotels under the Marriott, Hilton, and IHG brands to bring it to more locations.

Folding is the first job. Next are restocking housekeeping carts and moving linens between floors. We’re Archer, Daniel, Katherine, and Pranav, and we’re building robots that can learn to do routine physical work across industries.
one_liner: Robotics workforce for hotels
